componentAcceptance: All T26 criteria are covered by real Playwright. Temporary Bot/task contexts keep cookies and state apart, cross-owner sessions are denied and browser_close reclaims the session. An operator-approved profileId uses launchPersistentContext with a per-client/Bot/profile hashed data directory: the same Bot retains cookies across attempts, while another Bot using the same profile name starts empty. Downloads are scoped to the original session, capped at 1 MiB, returned with bytes and SHA-256, deleted after consumption and unavailable to another Bot.
productAcceptance: T26 passes at integration level. Login state, cookies and downloads do not leak between Bots; nonpersistent tasks are reclaimed and persistent profiles require explicit selection. Formal scores are 0/20 work packages, 28/63 scenarios and M0 11/12.
implementation: Added optional browserProfiles operator configuration and explicit browser_open profileId selection, partitioned by client/Bot/profile hash.
Nonpersistent contexts close completely; persistent sessions close only their page and retain the selected per-Bot context until Agent shutdown.
Added browser_download with session ownership, 1 MiB cap, SHA-256, one-time consumption and no cross-Bot lookup.
testRuns: npm run integration:probe-remote-agent-browser: all nine checks pass on Win11 Node24 with Chromium 156.0.8078.4.

Real assertions cover cookie isolation, cross-owner denial, close reclamation, persistent profile across attempt IDs, empty state for another Bot with the same profile name, and scoped one-time download bytes.
Final npm test: phase one 1593/1589/0/4 and phase two 387/303/0/84; total 1980 tests, 1892 pass, 0 fail, 88 skipped. npm run check:client: OK.
preservedFailures: The first persistent reopen checked a download page that had no cookie-state element; the fixture now exposes the same state probe there.
Repeated/cross-Bot download attempts return operation-level failed receipts rather than thrown errors; assertions now check the actual protocol shape.
limitations: The local browser executable may differ from a future distribution-pinned build. OS dependency installation remains a deployment gate.
Script and upload APIs remain T27 work. No production browser profile, real account, real model inference, push or release was used.
